cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.title: Bright Scarf Slow Track
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.ageModifications: Infant 0–6 months (younger: look only; older: may bat scarf)
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.objective: Support slow visual tracking with a bright moving scarf.
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.description: Baby watches a large bright scarf move slowly across their view while you name the color in a calm voice.
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.preparation:
Choose one high-contrast bright color
Clear visual clutter behind you
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.setup: Place baby comfortably on back or supported side on a mat.
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.steps:
1. Settle baby and gain eye contact first
2. Hold scarf about 8–12 inches away
3. Move slowly left, pause, then right
4. Name the color once or twice
5. Stop when baby looks away
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.teacherLanguage: Look… see the bright red? Watching… watching.
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.observationOpportunities: Tracks scarf briefly; stays calm while looking.
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.safetyNotes: Keep scarf away from face/neck; never leave draped on baby.
teacherTips: Slower than you think — pause when eyes lock on.

substitutions.use: large solid-color cloth napkin

observationPrompts: Tracks scarf briefly; stays calm while looking.
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.adaptations: Younger infants: shorter looking time, closer visuals, more face-to-face. Pause at gaze aversion.
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.extensions: If baby stays alert, offer one more brief repetition or a second color/pattern.
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.mixedAgeAdaptations: Birth–3 months: looking/listening focus. 3–6 months: invite reaching/grasping when ready.
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.imageBriefSetup: Caregiver kneeling on mat holding one bright scarf 8–12 inches from infant on back.
cur-act-9f2dd05998d64f68.outdoorAlternatives: If weather and shade allow, offer a brief outdoor version with the same materials.

cur-act-7bb994a0b2702459.title: Colorful Tummy Time Look

cur-act-7bb994a0b2702459.objective: Encourage head lifting during awake tummy time with a colorful visual anchor.
cur-act-7bb994a0b2702459.description: During supervised tummy time, a bright toy or cloth sits in view to invite looking and brief head lifts.
cur-act-7bb994a0b2702459.materials:
Tummy-time mat
1 large bright toy or cloth
Optional support roll
cur-act-7bb994a0b2702459.preparation:
Place colorful item at eye level in front of baby
Set timer mindset for short bursts
cur-act-7bb994a0b2702459.setup: Awake baby on tummy on firm mat; colorful item in front.

2. Set bright item in easy view
3. Get face-to-face beside baby and talk
4. Celebrate any head lift or looking
5. Return to back for rest as needed

cur-act-7bb994a0b2702459.safetyNotes: Tummy time only when awake and supervised. Back to sleep.

cur-act-b24cb49cd60df2a9.title: Face-to-Face Color Talk
cur-act-b24cb49cd60df2a9.objective: Connect caregiver face (best early visual target) with a simple color prop.
cur-act-b24cb49cd60df2a9.description: You hold baby close, smile, and slowly show one bright cloth while talking. Faces stay the main focus.
cur-act-b24cb49cd60df2a9.preparation: Sit where light falls on your face, not in baby’s eyes
cur-act-b24cb49cd60df2a9.setup: Hold baby 8–12 inches from your face with cloth nearby.
cur-act-b24cb49cd60df2a9.steps:
1. Gain eye contact and smile
2. Show cloth beside your face briefly
3. Name the color in a soft voice
4. Hide cloth and return to face play
5. End with a cuddle
cur-act-b24cb49cd60df2a9.teacherLanguage: Hi! I see you. Here is soft blue.
cur-act-b24cb49cd60df2a9.observationOpportunities: Looks at face; glances toward cloth.
cur-act-b24cb49cd60df2a9.safetyNotes: Support head/neck; stop if baby turns away.
cur-act-b24cb49cd60df2a9.cleanupTips: Set cloth aside for wash if mouthed.
teacherTips: Face first, prop second — never replace interaction with objects.

substitutions.use: large soft household cloth or board book with bold visuals

cur-act-6371165b47a34204.title: One-Color Slow Track
cur-act-6371165b47a34204.objective: Practice tracking with a single bold color to reduce visual overload.
cur-act-6371165b47a34204.description: Baby watches one solid-color scarf move slowly while you pause for focus.
cur-act-6371165b47a34204.materials:
One solid bright scarf
Mat
Support pillow if needed
cur-act-6371165b47a34204.preparation: Remove other bright toys from view
cur-act-6371165b47a34204.setup: Baby on back or side; one scarf only.
cur-act-6371165b47a34204.steps:
1. Show still scarf first
2. Move slowly side to side
3. Pause when baby fixates
4. Name color once
5. Rest
cur-act-6371165b47a34204.safetyNotes: Arm’s reach; no scarf near neck.
teacherTips: One color beats a rainbow pile for young infants.

substitutions.use: large soft household cloth or board book with bold visuals

cur-act-bcf9bf3a89dd426f.title: Color Cloth Touch Basket

week.weeklyOverview: This week focuses on looking, tracking, reaching, and warm caregiver talk with bright colors — not naming drills or crafts. Younger infants mostly look and listen; older infants may reach and grasp when ready.
week.objectives:
Support visual attention and slow tracking with bright, simple materials
Offer supervised tummy-time looking with colorful anchors
Encourage reaching/grasping only when developmentally ready
Build connection through face-to-face talk and short songs
Share brief, visually clear board-book moments
week.weeklyMaterials:
Large bright scarves (chiffon or soft fabric)
Soft colored cloth squares (too large to choke)
Baby-safe mirror
Large soft colored rattles/balls
Tummy-time mat
Simple color board books
Support pillow/roll for positioning
week.familyConnection: Invite families to name one bright color during a diaper change or walk — keep it playful, not a quiz.
week.adaptations: Younger infants: closer, slower, shorter. Older infants: offer graspable large toys. Reduce stimulation if baby looks away.
